subject: Post-call recap: FleetPay discovery — TCO levers & next steps
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.k@fleetpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-14T17:12:00Z
Subject: Post-call recap: FleetPay discovery — TCO levers & next steps

Samir — thanks for the time today. Quick recap while it's fresh and to make sure we aligned on the key constraints and possible levers for a pilot. Please flag any inaccuracies.

Highlights / pain we heard
- Cost pressure: Q3 integration budget is tight; you mentioned guidance of low-six-figures for experimentation, with strict procurement windows.
- Latency SLAs: product team wants ~200ms p95 for chat flows (initial prompt + 1–3 turn context).
- Token velocity: average session ~420 tokens, peak concurrency ~120 rps during peak batch.
- Quality tolerance: can accept small quality deltas for model variants, but not for critical reconciliation screens.

TCO levers we discussed (initial estimates in attached workbook)
- Batching: continuous batching for async flows can reduce per-token cost 20–40% depending on session spread; synchronous chat batching gains are smaller but still meaningful.
- KV/prefix caching: reuse of repeated prompts (merchant lookups) could cut effective token send by 10–30% for targeted routes.
- Model routing: route low-risk flows to a cheaper quantized model; keep sensitive flows on the larger model. Potential 2–3x cost delta across variants.
- Reserved capacity / commit discounts: a short reserved commit for Dedicated during pilot to stabilize unit costs — we showed a 15–25% delta versus pure on-demand in the workbook.
- Quantization tradeoffs: 4-bit quantization reduces GPU cost significantly; need to validate quality on your eval set.

Proposed pilot scope (lightweight)
- 30-day pilot, focus on 3 routes: merchant chat, dispute triage, reconciliation assistant.
- Target volume: ~5M tokens/month to start (we modeled ranges in the workbook).
- Metrics: cost per 1k tokens, p95 latency, accuracy on reconciliation prompts (we'll derive a small eval set).

Next steps
1) We'll share the TCO workbook + a draft scope (attached). Ben will add a short note on batching assumptions.
2) Can you confirm procurement window and target PO cadence? You mentioned July PO window — is that the right target for pilot funding?
3) If procurement is OK, we'd aim to kick off pilot week of 2026-07-06.
4) Please add any procurement contacts so we can loop them in with a price sheet and MSA.

Attachments: FleetPay_TCO_workbook.xlsx (estimates), pilot_scope_draft.pdf (scope + success criteria), redwood-pilot-price-sheet.xlsx

Thanks — will follow up with Ben's technical assumptions later today.

— Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Sales Lead, Payments & Fintech
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: FleetPay discovery — TCO levers & next steps

Evelyn — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Budget: our initial Q3 experimental budget is ~$75,000. That won't cover large reserved commits but could cover a small-dedicated pilot or a hosted pilot with a committed token bucket.
- SLOs: 200ms p95 is our aspirational target for the merchant chat path; for dispute triage we can accept up to 400ms p95.
- Volume: the 5M tokens/month looks reasonable as a mid-range estimate. Peak concurrency note — the 120 rps was for a one-off flash sale pattern; average concurrency is closer to 25–40 rps.
- Quality/quantization: interested in a short eval to measure quality delta from 8-bit -> 4-bit quant. Who on your team would own that evaluation? Also, we need to see any degradation examples for reconciliation flows before we commit.

Procurement: looping in procurement above. Procurement — we need: price sheet, SOW skeleton, and MSA redlines. If those docs arrive this week, we can try to make the July window.

Thanks — Samir

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: FleetPay discovery — TCO levers & next steps (technical assumptions)

Samir / team — quick tech note to attach to the workbook and scope. These are our assumptions and the numbers we used in the cost model: please call out anything you think is off.

1) Batching assumptions- Async background flows: 75–85% batching efficiency (clients with flexible latency) -> modeled as 40% per-token cost reduction.- Sync chat: with short windows we used 10–25% effective batching depending on how long you hold requests (we can tune this at the edge).

2) Caching / KV reuse- We modeled reuse rates of 15% (conservative) to 35% (aggressive) based on merchant lookup reuse. This is route-dependent — recommend instrumenting 2–3 days of real traffic to baseline.

3) Quantization impact- 8-bit -> 4-bit: expect 1.5–2.2x perf improvement on GPU memory and cost; quality delta depends on prompt sensitivity. We'll run ~200 reconciliation prompts and provide a short report.

4) Model routing and fallback- Pilot config: route merchant chat and FAQ to quantized-moderate model; route reconciliation assistant to higher-fidelity model. On capacity events we'll fallback to hosted smaller model (graceful degrade).

5) Latency expectations- With dedicated pools and short-context optimization we expect 120–220ms p95 for the cheaper model under normal load; the higher-fidelity path will be ~200–350ms p95 depending on sequence length. We'll instrument p95 at token boundary so you get per-route metrics.

6) Ops & instrumentation- We'll ship a small agent that emits token-level cost, route-level latency, and a quality sampling hook for reconciliation prompts. We prefer to use the shared Drive link for automated uploads of eval sets.

I'll drop a trimmed assumptions page into the workbook and share an updated price sheet.

— Ben
